AgentSpec — Programming Autonomous Agents Contents Cheatsheet

A declaration language and its toolchain

AgentSpec
Programming Autonomous Agents

Eleven chapters Voice: The Crafter Set in Swiss

An agent that runs while you sleep will meet a case you did not anticipate, and it will decide something. AgentSpec is a specification language for that moment: the routine's judgment stays in the model, and the routine's boundaries move into a file that is valid Python, never executed, and read directly by the agent as its instruction.

The other half of the system is a static toolchain — aspec — that lints the same file, derives its execution waves, draws its failure paths, simulates its untaken branches, and tells you in CI when a pull request has just given a bot merge rights. This book builds the language a piece at a time and then reads a real routine that has been corrected three times by production.

There is also a cheatsheet — the language and the CLI on one page, for when you are writing a spec rather than learning one.
